first.text:
My recommendation is 10.

The week as written gives the pull-up 11 hard sets: 3 negatives and 4 band sets on Wednesday, 3 band sets on Sunday, and Friday's strict single. A target of 11 means a single dropped set on a tired evening reads as a shortfall, which is noise. A target of 8 is still met when Wednesday is lost entirely, and Wednesday is the pull-up day, so that is exactly the week I want to hear about. 10 sits between: one set of slack for a bad day, no cover for a missed session. It also matches the 10 hard sets every other muscle is held to, so the pull-up is asked for the same work as the rest of the body, not a token. If the band and negative work later shrinks because strict reps become real sets, the target moves with it.

Deadlift as agreed: the target stays at 4, acknowledged on the record that Sunday's top set and three back-offs are the planned hinge work and Friday's Romanian deadlift carries the rest of the pattern.

Say yes to 10 and I'll put the deadlift note in, show you the fresh dry run with every flag, and adopt only on your go. Publishing stays off until the kit tables are done.
